title: Add streaming/tool-call observability counters for example smoke tests
author: Sahana Iyer
release_notes:
- Internal: emit lightweight counters for streaming disconnects and partial tool-call args to make example smoke tests regression-resistant.
- No API behavior changes; metrics are additive and behind the existing metrics export.
description:
Context: The examples refresh work (ENG-4821/4822) is adding golden transcripts + smoke tests that exercise streaming, tool calling, and structured output. We’ve had a few regressions slip through because the test harness could only assert on final text (or brittle event ordering) and didn’t have a stable signal when certain edge cases occurred (disconnect mid-stream, partial tool args emitted across multiple chunks, etc.). This PR adds a small set of counters in the API gateway streaming path and tool-call assembly code so smoke tests can assert “did we observe the expected condition?” without coupling to internal event serialization.

What’s included: (1) New Prometheus counters (namespaced under redwood_api_*) emitted from the streaming SSE/WebSocket handlers and tool-call delta assembler: redwood_api_stream_disconnect_total{reason}, redwood_api_stream_reconnect_total{success}, redwood_api_tool_call_partial_args_total{tool_name}, redwood_api_stream_parse_error_total{stage}, redwood_api_stream_final_message_assembled_total{mode}. (2) A tiny test-only “metrics snapshot” helper used by the examples smoke tests to read counter deltas between test phases (no dependency on internal tracing; works in local + CI). (3) Documentation in the smoke test README on how to interpret these metrics when debugging flakes.

Design notes / constraints: Metrics are intentionally low-cardinality. tool_name is capped to a short allowlist in the example runner (unknown tools bucket to tool_name="other"). We only increment tool_call_partial_args when we see arguments delivered over >1 delta chunk for a single call_id (this directly targets SUP-18421 confusion). The disconnect counter is best-effort and increments on any transport close before the terminal event is emitted; it should not be used as a billing/usage signal.

Testing: Added unit tests around the delta assembler to ensure partial-args detection increments once per call_id. Added integration coverage in the example smoke test harness to assert counters change as expected during a forced disconnect/retry scenario. Ran existing gateway tests + examples suite.

Impact: No user-facing API changes. Adds a few counters to the existing metrics endpoint. Helps catch regressions earlier (especially around the known pitfalls section in the refreshed docs).
commits: metrics: add streaming disconnect/reconnect counters in gateway handlers
metrics: increment tool_call_partial_args in tool-call delta assembler
tests: add unit tests for partial-args detection and counter increments
examples/ci: add metrics snapshot helper + smoke-test assertions
docs: update example smoke test README with debugging notes
conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Can we keep label cardinality low? tool_name could explode if customers define arbitrary tools.

Sahana Iyer (author): Yep — tool_name label is only used by the examples runner. In gateway/runtime we only emit tool_name for known example tools; everything else buckets to "other". Added a note + guard in the helper.
Brian Murphy: For stream_disconnect, do we risk double-counting when the client cancels after completion but before we flush the terminal event?

Sahana Iyer (author): Good call. I changed the increment to only happen when we have not emitted terminal_event=true for that request context. Added a unit test for “graceful finish then close” to ensure no increment.
Sabrina James: Smoke test expectation: should we assert exact counts or just >0? Concerned about retries changing counts.
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated the smoke tests to assert minimum deltas (>=1) for disconnect/reconnect and exact-once for partial_args per call_id. That should be stable even with additional retries.
Connor O'Brien: Any rollout concerns for metrics dashboards/alerts?
Sahana Iyer (author): No alerts added. These are purely counters; we can decide later if SRE wants alerting. Documented them under “example validation metrics” only.
